description.narrative: Support to Transparency Intern to implement the strategy Holding Power to Account: Impact: African countries’ ability to raise domestic resources and channel public funds toward development outcomes is enhanced through improved safeguards against corruption and illicit financial flows. Outcomes:(1) African countries commit to and embed anti-corruption and financial integrity in domestic frameworks governing resource mobilization and allocation. 2) Multilateral fora and standard-setting bodies adopt priority measures to support African countries in reducing resource leakages and illicit financial flows Intermediate outcomes: 1. Policy discourse on domestic resource mobilization in target countries is enhanced through the integration of anti-corruption and financial integrity perspectives. 2. National ownership of priority anti-corruption and financial integrity measures increases across Africa. 3. Global policy debates increasingly focus on anti-corruption and financial integrity measures that can help address the development needs of African countries. Immediate outcomes: 1. An expanded evidence base informs understanding of how corruption undermines domestic resource mobilization and distorts public resource allocation in Africa. 2. Civil society in target countries plays a stronger role in policy debates on domestic resource mobilization and allocation by building coalitions and promoting anti-corruption and financial integrity measures. 3. Civil society across Africa has increased opportunities to advocate for anti-corruption and financial integrity measures in multilateral fora. 4. Civil society advocacy for anti-corruption and financial integrity in multilateral fora is bolstered by evidence and targeted recommendations that reflect Africa's development perspectives. Target group: civil society in target countries: Gambia, Ghana, Mauritius, Nigeria, South Africa and Rwanda and representatives and government delegates in multilateral bodies.
